introduction.heading: Plumbing for Centerville homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Centerville were built in 1987 or later, and about 38% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

About two-thirds of Centerville's drinking water comes from seven deep city wells. The rest is treated water bought from the Weber Basin Water Conservancy District, which starts mostly as Weber River surface water.

Outdoor watering in Centerville uses separate secondary water from Weber Basin or the Deuel Creek irrigation system, each with its own watering days.
